papers.title: Heterogeneity in excess respiratory acute care utilization during wildfire smoke waves in California
papers.abstract: Rationale: Wildfire smoke is an increasing public health threat, yet most epidemiologic studies estimate average smoke-health associations across broad spatial or temporal scales. Such approaches may obscure substantial heterogeneity across individual smoke waves, leaving an important evidence gap for dynamic public health preparedness, risk communication, and clinical practice. Objectives: To estimate event-specific excess respiratory acute care utilization during smoke waves and identify smoke wave features associated with higher excess utilization. Methods: We conducted a statewide study of 18,271,754 respiratory acute care encounters in California from 2006 to 2019. A smoke wave was defined as at least 2 consecutive days during which county-level wildfire smoke fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exceeded the 95th percentile over the study period. We applied a machine learning-integrated two-stage interrupted time-series design to estimate excess respiratory acute care utilization during each event. We then used meta-regressions to examine multiple spatiotemporally varying effect modifiers such as smoke wave duration, intensity, timing, and co-occurring climate and meteorological conditions. Measurements and Main Results: A total of 1,249 smoke waves were identified and examined in this study. Excess respiratory acute care utilization varied substantially across smoke waves. Higher excess utilization was associated with longer smoke wave duration, greater intensity, winter occurrence, short recovery period, overlap with holidays, drought conditions, or co-occurrence with precipitation or extreme heat events. Conclusions: This study proposes a novel analytical framework to systematically evaluate spatiotemporal drivers of heterogeneity in wildfire smoke respiratory health effects. The findings can inform dynamic preparedness and public health response to smoke events.

papers.title: Tuberculosis Severity metrics poorly predict Two-Month Culture Conversion
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives Among people with pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB), culture conversion (bacterial clearance) after two months of treatment is a critical indicator of response. However, predictors of culture conversion at two months are difficult to define and can be context specific. In this study, we evaluated how well two tuberculosis (TB) severity metrics, the chest Xray (CXR) Score and the Bandim TBScore associate with and predict two-month culture conversion. Methods The cohort contained 718 index PTB cases enrolled in The Kawempe Community Health Study (KCHS). We analyzed severity metrics, demographics, clinical, microbiological, radiological, household and behavioral data for their association with and their ability to predict culture conversion. Results Sixty-eight percent of participants culture converted at two months. The highest CXR Score category (odds ratio (OR) 0.51, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) 0.31, 0.84), smear grade at diagnosis (OR 0.42, 95% CI; 0.26, 0.62), pleural thickening (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.17, 0.95) and current smoking (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.09, 0.99) inversely associated with conversion. Both severity measures and the most parsimonious model poorly predicted culture conversion (all AUCs<0.70). Conclusion CXR Score, higher smear grade at diagnosis, pleural thickening, and current smoking inversely associated with culture conversion but provided limited utility for prediction. Keywords: Tuberculosis outcomes; Mycobacterium clearance; TB severity scores

papers.title: Environmental Chemical and Psychosocial Stress Exposures during Pregnancy and Child Behavioral Problems through 10 Years of Age in a South African Birth Cohort
papers.abstract: Introduction: Prenatal exposure to environmental chemicals and psychosocial stress often co-occur in low- and middle-income settings, yet their joint effects on child behavior from preschool to school-age remain unknown. We investigated the joint associations of prenatal chemical metabolites and psychosocial stress on child behavior in the first decade of life in the South African birth cohort, the Drakenstein Child Health Study. Methods: Among 643 mother-child pairs, we quantified 25 chemical metabolites spanning nine classes (organophosphates, pyrethroids, neonicotinoid, chlorinated phenol, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, parabens, bisphenols, UV filters, other biocides) in second-trimester maternal urine and characterized prenatal psychosocial stress as a five-indicator latent construct using confirmatory factor analysis. Internalizing and externalizing problems were assessed with the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) at 2, 3.5, 5, 6.5, 8, and 10 years. We fit adjusted generalized estimating equations for single exposures with false discovery rate correction. We assessed the joint effects of the positively associated exposure classes using quantile-based g-computation (QG-COMP). Models were fit separately in the preschool (2 to 5 years) and school-age (6.5 to 10 years) developmental windows. Finally, we tested effect measure modification by maternal psychosocial stress and by child sex. Results: Chemical associations were confined to the preschool window. Three polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) metabolites were associated with increased externalizing problems (2-hydroxyfluorene 1.49 [95% CI 0.37, 2.60]; 1-naphthol 1.14 [0.21, 2.07]; 1-hydroxypyrene 1.05 [0.14, 1.95]), as was the PAH mixture (externalizing {psi}=1.00 [0.32, 1.68]; internalizing {psi}=0.95 [0.26, 1.64]). Psychosocial associations persisted across both windows (e.g. latent stress score and externalizing problems: 1.52 [0.83, 2.22] preschool, 1.45 [0.77, 2.14] school-age). The joint PAH and psychosocial mixture showed the largest effects at preschool (externalizing {psi}=2.15 [1.15, 3.15]; internalizing {psi}=2.02 [0.98, 3.06]), with psychosocial factors contributing most to the joint effect. Preschool associations were present among boys, but not girls (joint mixture, externalizing: {psi}=3.42 [2.09, 4.69] in boys versus 0.74 [-0.67, 2.14] in girls, interaction p=0.004). There was no evidence of modification by maternal psychosocial stress. Discussion: Prenatal urinary PAH metabolite levels and psychosocial exposures were associated with child behavioral problems through distinct developmental courses, with PAH associations limited to early childhood and psychosocial associations persisting into the school-age years. Their joint effect exceeded that of either domain alone, and was heightened among boys during the preschool years. These findings highlight the importance of joint chemical and non-chemical stressors on child mental health.

papers.title: DYCAST early warning system for dengue virus risk areas, Ribeirao Preto, Brazil
papers.abstract: Dengue is currently the fastest-spreading vector-borne disease, with an estimated 100-400 million infections per year and nearly 6 billion people at risk--more than half the world's population. However, there is no specific antiviral treatment, thus the primary method for preventing infection is through targeted control of the principal mosquito vector, Aedes aegypti. The objective of this retrospective study is to evaluate the efficacy of forecasting dengue risk using human cases and an adaptation of DYCAST: a biologically based, spatiotemporal clustering model that proved operationally successful as a West Nile virus early warning system. Results demonstrate that DYCAST provided accurate and early detection of high-risk areas for dengue in Ribeirao Preto, Brazil, including a cryptic interepidemic focus of transmission preceding a severe epidemic. Using suspected cases, DYCAST predicted 90.3% (4,237/4,690) of confirmed cases, with a mean lead time of 66.3 days prior to illness onset. High-risk cells had >10x higher relative risk of containing a confirmed case, and sensitivity and specificity were 83.8% and 72.3%. These findings suggest that DYCAST could be utilized in real time to prospectively identify areas at high risk of dengue, for rapid and precise targeting of mosquito mitigation and public education. Implementation using free, open-source software offers a scalable technological strategy for the prevention and control of dengue around the world.

papers.title: Epidemiology of Cardiac Structure and Function Among African Caribbeans in Tobago: A Population-based Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Background: Individuals of African genetic ancestry are at high risk for heart failure (HF), which is often preceded by cardiac structural and functional abnormalities. Nevertheless, little is known about cardiac structure and function among Afro-Caribbeans residing in Tobago. This study aimed to investigate the epidemiology of cardiac structure and function among African Caribbeans in Tobago. Methods: A total of 924 participants (41-83 years) underwent clinical evaluation and transthoracic echocardiography. Images were analyzed for left ventricular (LV) mass index (MI), left atrial volume index, diastolic dysfunction (DD), LV ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e' ratio, E/A ratio, and other echocardiographic measures. Cardiac structure and function were evaluated by age, sex, and HF stage. Results: The mean age was 61.7 years, with 61.4% women, 47.8% obesity, and 20.2% diabetes. Average systolic blood pressure was approximately 140 mmHg, and 76.7% had hypertension. Abnormal LV geometry was present in 77.1% of participants, predominantly concentric remodeling (69.5%). The prevalence of DD was 13.4%, LVEF <50% was 1.5%, and abnormal GLS ([≤]-18%) was 5.2%. Women had significantly higher E/e' ratios and a higher prevalence of Stage A and Stage B HF, whereas men had a higher prevalence of symptomatic (Stage C) HF. Participants aged 65-83 years had significantly higher E/e' ratio, concentric remodeling, and LV hypertrophy than those aged 41-57 years. Conclusions: Women and older adults have higher LV structural abnormalities and DD than men and younger adults. These results will be helpful to inform public health priorities related to cardiovascular health in Tobago.

papers.title: Depressive Symptom Trajectories and Incident Cognitive Impairment by Outcome Ascertainment
papers.abstract: Importance: Dementia prevention frameworks treat depression as a leading modifiable risk factor, but cohort estimates of the association vary widely; whether this variation reflects how cognitive outcomes are ascertained is unknown. Objective: To examine whether associations between depressive symptom trajectories and incident cognitive impairment vary by outcome ascertainment rigor. Design, Setting, and Participants: This harmonized cohort study included 91,043 adults aged 50 years or older from 4 national longitudinal aging cohorts (CHARLS [China], HRS [US], ELSA [England], and SHARE [16 European countries]); baseline waves spanned 2006 to 2011, with follow-up through 2023. Exposure: Depressive symptom trajectory classes (persistent low, persistent high, incident worsening, remitting) derived using group-based trajectory modeling. Main Outcomes and Measures: Incident cognitive impairment ascertained under a 5-level hierarchy of increasing rigor, from self-report (level 1) to clinical consensus diagnosis (level 5; Harmonized Cognitive Assessment Protocol [HCAP]). Cohort-specific Cox models were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis; meta-regression tested ascertainment rigor as a moderator of heterogeneity. Results: Under nonadjudicated outcomes, the incident-worsening trajectory was associated with incident cognitive impairment in CHARLS (HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.06-1.62) and SHARE (HR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.87-2.13) but not HRS (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.95-1.16) or ELSA (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.95-1.27); the persistent-high trajectory was not significant under any nonadjudicated outcome (HR range, 1.07-1.15). Under clinical consensus diagnosis (n = 3,196), all non-low trajectories were independently associated with mild cognitive impairment or dementia (OR range, 1.66-2.29; dementia-only persistent high: OR, 3.32; 95% CI, 1.85-5.95). Effect sizes increased stepwise with ascertainment rigor (meta-regression slope, 0.314 log HR per level; P < .001; residual I2 = 0%; R2 = 100%; exploratory). Findings were robust to lagged, weighted, and competing-risk analyses; biological aging acceleration did not differ across trajectories. Conclusions and Relevance: The detectability and magnitude of depression-related cognitive risk depend on outcome ascertainment rigor. Prevention trials and burden projections relying on self-reported outcomes may underestimate the benefit of depression treatment.

papers.title: Elevated maternal hemoglobin levels during pregnancy are associated with autism spectrum disorder in the offspring: A population-based cohort study
papers.abstract: BackgroundAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) is an increasingly prevalent neurodevelopmental condition with multifactorial origins, including potential prenatal environmental contributions. Maternal anemia (decreased hemoglobin [Hb] levels) has long been associated with adverse offspring neurodevelopmental outcomes, yet evidence regarding elevated levels of antenatal hemoglobin levels, in relation to ASD risk remains limited. This study evaluated the association between maternal Hb levels during pregnancy and the risk of ASD diagnosis in offspring. MethodsThis large-scale, population-based retrospective cohort study used electronic health records from births of members of Clalit Health Services (CHS), the largest health maintenance organization in Israel, between 2011 and 2021. The study included 303,234 singleton live births to Jewish mothers who had at least one measured prenatal Hb value and were CHS members. Exclusion criteria were children with known genetic disorders and births 97.5th percentile). The main outcome was a diagnosis of ASD in the offspring, as recorded in medical files. Statistical analyses adjusted for maternal age, socioeconomic status, gestational diabetes, BMI, and other clinical and demographic factors. ResultsAmong the 303,234 births, 8,106 (2.7%) children were diagnosed with ASD. High maternal Hb levels were associated with elevated odds of ASD diagnosis (aOR=1.22; 95% CI=1.08-1.37), with the strongest association observed for first-trimester measurements (aOR=1.31; 95% CI=1.14-1.49). This association persisted in the sibling-matched analysis (aOR=1.64; 95% CI=1.08-2.47) and was not modified by maternal RBC levels, suggesting that it was not explained by familial factors or RBC counts. The main limitations of this study include the lack of available data on maternal smoking, and the absence of detailed information on maternal nutritional status. ConclusionsThese findings suggest that elevated antenatal Hb levels may be relevant to offspring neurodevelopment. Further studies are needed to replicate these findings and clarify the biological mechanisms underlying this association.

papers.title: Chronic Maternal White Blood Cell Elevation During Pregnancy and Offspring Autism
papers.abstract: Background: Maternal immune activation is a robust risk factor for autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Current evidence relies on specialized immunological markers not routinely measured, limiting population-level risk identification. We investigated the association between maternal white blood cell (WBC) counts, a ubiquitous component of routine prenatal care during pregnancy, and offspring ASD risk. Methods: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study of 303,234 singleton live births (51% male) between 2011 and 2021 from Clalit Health Services in Israel. Exposures were maternal total and differential WBC counts from routine testing during the 1st and 2nd trimesters. High and low exposures were defined as >97.5th and <2.5th percentiles, respectively. The primary outcome was clinical ASD diagnosis. Analyses included multivariable logistic regressions, matched-sibling analyses (n=2,894 discordant pairs), and chronicity analyses in multiparous mothers (n=72,102). Results: Among 303,234 children, 8,106 (2.7%) were diagnosed with ASD. Elevated maternal total WBC counts were associated with increased odds of ASD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=1.59; 95% CI, 1.43-1.75), with the strongest association in the 1st trimester (aOR=1.64; 95% CI, 1.45-1.85). Similar associations were seen with elevated neutrophils, lymphocytes, and monocytes. While most associations were attenuated in matched-sibling analyses, chronicity analysis revealed increased ASD odds in offspring of mothers with persistently elevated WBC counts across multiple pregnancies (aOR=1.49; 95% CI, 1.08-2.01). Conclusions: Persistently elevated maternal WBC counts across pregnancies are associated with increased offspring ASD risk. These routinely collected hematologic markers support the maternal immune activation hypothesis and may contribute to future prenatal risk assessment models.

papers.title: The health and wellbeing impact of arts engagement: A longitudinal outcome-wide approach in 22 countries
papers.abstract: Arts and cultural engagement is increasingly recognised as a potential resource for health and wellbeing, yet evidence remains dominated by Western, high-income countries. Using data from the Global Flourishing Study across 22 countries (N=118,045), we examined associations between arts engagement and 19 health and wellbeing outcomes across five domains, applying an outcome-wide analytical framework and random-effects meta-analysis. Arts engagement was consistently associated with greater positive wellbeing and character strengths, higher evaluative wellbeing, and better social and general health, including lower loneliness. By contrast, associations with future-oriented wellbeing and perceived capability were less robust, and no pooled associations emerged for psychological distress. Country-level characteristics explained little cross-national variation. These findings suggest that arts engagement may promote flourishing across diverse cultural contexts, with benefits extending beyond the prevention of psychological distress, highlighting its potential role as a global population health resource.

papers.title: Childhood and adolescent cancer diagnosis, treatment, and hospitalizations during the COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec, Canada, a population-based study
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare delivery globally. In Quebec, Canada, measures were introduced to prioritize pediatric oncology care. Using administrative data, we estimated pandemic-related changes in cancer diagnoses, treatments, and length of hospital stay among individuals aged 0-19 in Quebec (2015-2023). Interrupted time series analyses using autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models assessed immediate and sustained changes in monthly age-standardized rates of diagnoses, treatments (chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy-related encounters), positron emission tomography scans, and hospital admissions. Separate ARIMA models fitted to pre-pandemic monthly counts generated counterfactual forecasts to estimate the cumulative differences between observed and expected diagnoses and treatments over 3, 12, and 46 months of the pandemic. Generalized linear mixed models assessed changes in length of stay between the pre- and post-pandemic periods and whether these changes differed by patient characteristics. We identified 2,570 patients: 1,475 diagnosed through February 2020 and 1,095 from March 2020 onward. We found no evidence of immediate or sustained changes in monthly incidence rates. Cumulative diagnoses and treatments remained within expected levels across periods, although estimates were imprecise. For diagnoses, the 3-, 12-, and 46-month cumulative differences were -1 (95% uncertainty interval [UI] -17 to 15), 24 (95% UI, -9 to 57), and 2 (95% UI, -94 to 96), respectively. Changes in length of hospital stay varied across subgroups, although their clinical significance remains uncertain. Pediatric cancer diagnosis and treatment activity was largely maintained across Quebec throughout the pandemic, consistent with the objectives of provincial and institutional measures to preserve pediatric oncology services.

papers.title: Improving UK Biobank algorithms for Parkinson's disease ascertainment using drug claims
papers.abstract: Background: Accurate ascertainment of Parkinson's disease (PD) is a major challenge in large-scale epidemiological studies. The UK Biobank (UKB) is widely used for PD research, but ascertainment based on hospital and death records may result in misclassification and delayed PD diagnoses. Objectives: We compared different strategies for ascertaining PD in the UKB, and examined their impact on incidence and associations with risk factors and mortality. Methods: We compared PD ascertained through hospital and death records (ADO-PD) to two approaches that rely on primary care data available for ~45% of participants: diagnoses from general practitioner consultations (Clinical-PD); a novel drug-based algorithm (Drug-PD). We compared incidence, age at diagnosis, and associations with sex, walking speed, and mortality across all algorithms. Results: ADO-PD identified ~20% fewer prevalent and incident cases than Drug-PD over 15y of follow-up, and estimated age at diagnosis to be 4.2y (median) later than age at anti-PD drugs initiation. ADO-PD identified never treated participants or with other causes of parkinsonism as PD patients. While Drug-PD yielded incidence rates consistent with UK reference rates, ADO-PD underestimated incidence by 36% compared to reference rates. Associations with sex, walking speed, and mortality were significantly different for ADO-PD compared to Drug-PD. Clinical-PD and Drug-PD yielded similar findings, although Clinical-PD included patients with other causes of parkinsonism. Conclusions: We draw attention to methodological issues regarding PD ascertainment in the UKB and their consequences. These results can help inform strategies for PD ascertainment by combining multiple data sources, thereby improving the validity of epidemiological analyses.

papers.title: Modeling spontaneous hepatitis C virus clearance by age, sex, IFNL4 genotype, and infection history: Implications for simulations of elimination and vaccine trials
papers.abstract: Background and Aims: The probability of hepatitis C virus (HCV) clearance is mediated by an interaction between numerous factors. However, variation in spontaneous HCV clearance was previously modeled using relatively simple approaches with fixed probabilities by sex. Here, we developed a literature-informed clearance algorithm that considers age, sex, interferon lambda 4 (IFNL4) genotype, and infection history to model the probability of HCV clearance in vulnerable populations, such as people who inject drugs (PWID), and in controlled human infection (CHI) models for future HCV vaccines. Methods: We modeled HCV clearance probabilities for three infection-history pathways: first infection, reinfection after spontaneous clearance, and reinfection after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) cure. Logistic and cumulative-hazard equations assigned person-specific clearance probabilities in the first two pathways. The post-DAA pathway used fixed clearance probabilities. We tested the algorithm using HepCEP (Hepatitis C Elimination in PWID), an agent-based simulator. Results: First-infection clearance probabilities ranged from 0.13 to 0.51 across eight age, sex, and IFNL4 genotype subgroups. Clearance probabilities for reinfection after spontaneous clearance ranged from 0.20 to 0.80 at literature point estimates. Across 100 runs, the mean assigned clearance probabilities were 0.27 for first infections and 0.52 for reinfections after spontaneous clearance, compared with literature inputs of 0.26 and 0.52, respectively. Probabilities varied across subgroups and runs. Conclusion: Simulations reproduced the algorithm's intended clearance heterogeneity and uncertainty by age, sex, IFNL4 genotype, and infection history, which may support models of HCV elimination in vulnerable populations and CHI model development for future HCV vaccines.

papers.title: Perinatal suicide risk factors: A network analysis
papers.abstract: Purpose Suicide during pregnancy or after birth (the perinatal period) represents a leading, preventable cause of United States maternal deaths. This study aimed to understand the complex relationship between perinatal status and life circumstances among perinatal suicide decedents in the United States and generate insights regarding suicide risk. Methods This cross-sectional study used decedent data from the 2003-2023 National Violent Death Reporting System suicide mortality registry (N=20,217). We applied psychometric network analysis using 18 binary life circumstances indicators representing four domains: relationships, health, socioeconomic status, and risk factors for suicide. We generated two networks for the overall sample and perinatal sample and assessed network structure, bridge centralities, and stability. Results The analytic sample included 1,297 perinatal and 18,920 non-perinatal decedents. The network of the overall sample was stable. Perinatal status did not appear at the center of the network but connected primarily with intimate partner problems. The network of the perinatal sample was modestly stable. Postpartum status was not at the center of the network but connected to depressed mood and mental health diagnoses. In both networks, depressed mood had the highest bridge betweenness, and there was a consistent link between physical health domains and socioeconomic domains. Conclusion Suicide prevention strategies targeting childbearing-aged women should incorporate factors beyond pregnancy, including physical health, intimate partner relationships, and socioeconomic challenges.

papers.title: Validation of gender identity and sexual behavior stigma measures among transgender women in the United States: Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses
papers.abstract: Introduction Transgender women experience stigma related to both gender identity and sexual behavior, yet robust measurement tools remain limited. This study evaluated the factor structure and external construct validity of the Measures of Attributional Stigma for gender identity (MAS-GI) and sexual behavior (MAS-SB) among transgender women in the United States. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Transgender Womens Internet Survey and Testing (TWIST) platform collected from 2023-2025 (N=2,901). Participants completed parallel 14-item stigma measures attributed separately to gender identity and sexual behavior. The sample was split into exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n=1,951; 2023-2024) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n=950; 2024-2025) samples. External construct validity was evaluated via associations with depression symptoms, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), social capital, transgender identity pride, and healthcare utilization. Results EFA identified three MAS-GI factors (family stigma, anticipated healthcare stigma, and enacted social stigma) and two MAS-SB factors (global healthcare stigma and social/institutional stigma). CFA confirmed both structures with good to excellent model fit. All stigma dimensions were positively associated with depression and PTSD. Anticipated healthcare and enacted social stigma from the MAS-GI and both MAS-SB dimensions were negatively associated with social capital. Greater anticipated gender identity healthcare stigma associated with lower transgender identity pride. Several stigma dimensions were also positively associated with HIV/STI testing, PrEP use, and mental healthcare utilization. Conclusions The MAS-GI and MAS-SB demonstrate factorial validity and preliminary external construct validity among transgender women. These measures enable precise assessment of stigma by attribution and source and inform stigma surveillance and intervention evaluation.

papers.title: Moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, longitudinal blood pressure trajectories, and hypertension-related outcomes in older adults at high cardiovascular risk: a cohort study
papers.abstract: BackgroundWe aimed to investigate the association between moderate-to-vigorous leisure-time physical activity (MVLTPA) and longitudinal trajectories of systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) blood pressure, as well as the incidence of high blood pressure and antihypertensive drug initiation, in adults aged 60-80 years at high cardiovascular risk. MethodsIn participants from the PREDIMED trial (61% women; 5,254 participants), MVLTPA was assessed using the Minnesota Leisure Time Physical Activity Questionnaire and expressed as cumulative average metabolic equivalent of task{middle dot}minutes/day. SBP and DBP trajectories were modelled using mixed-effects models with cubic splines ([≥]100 [adequate] vs <100 [insufficient] metabolic equivalent of task{middle dot}minutes/day). First occurrence of high blood pressure (SBP [≥]140 mmHg or DBP [≥]90 mmHg) and antihypertensive drug initiation were assessed with Cox models (adequate vs insufficient, and continuous MVLTPA). ResultsSBP and DBP declined with increasing age, with no clinically meaningful differences between MVLTPA groups. The association between adequate MVLTPA and incident high blood pressure was null (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.94-1.32). However, adequate MVLTPA was associated with a 17% lower risk of antihypertensive drug initiation (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71-0.98). The association appeared stronger in women (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58-0.94) than in men (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.78-1.22) (p-value for sex interaction = 0.058). A modest inverse linear dose-response association between MVLTPA and risk of antihypertensive drug initiation was also observed (per 25 metabolic equivalent of task{middle dot}minutes/day: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p-value = 0.022). ConclusionsIn older adults at high cardiovascular risk, MVLTPA was not associated with clinically meaningful differences in SBP or DBP trajectories or incident high blood pressure, but was associated with a lower risk of antihypertensive drug initiation. These findings support promoting habitual physical activity as part of cardiovascular risk management in older adults. Trial registrationISRCTN35739639

papers.title: Sputum quality and diagnostic outcomes of GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay among adults with presumed tuberculosis in two district hospitals in Ghana: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Ghana, where GeneXpert MTB/RIF serves as a first-line diagnostic tool. However, uncertainties about this method persist regarding specimen quality and the clinical significance of indeterminate rifampicin susceptibility results. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of samples from 3,977 presumptive TB patients tested either at HopeXchange Medical Center (Kumasi) or Keta Municipal Hospital between January 2020 and December 2024. Demographic data, sputum macroscopic appearance, and GeneXpert results were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Fishers exact test. Results: Overall Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTb) test positivity was 11.6% (461/3977). Males accounted for 63.3% of positive results, with the highest percentage among those ages 30-40 years. Mucopurulent specimens yielded the highest positivity rate (25.4%), compared to 4.0% of salivary specimens. Blood-stained sputum specimens (n=44) showed a 15.9% positivity rate. Although confirmed rifampicin resistance was low (1.7%), 9.3% of all MTb positive samples yielded an indeterminate result. The rate of indeterminate results from samples collected at Kwadaso Municipal increased from 7.3% in 2021 to 28.6% in 2024. Conclusion: These findings validate Ghana National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) guidelines emphasizing the reliability of mucopurulent specimen collection, but challenges the routine rejection of blood-stained sputum. The rising trend of indeterminate rifampicin results requires further investigation of circulating rpoB mutation profiles and quality assurance measures. Patients with indeterminate results should be further assessed using drug susceptibility testing to rule out rifampicin resistance. The findings provide actionable evidence to refine diagnostic algorithms and improve TB care in Ghana.

papers.title: Surge and decline of typhoid fever before and after a typhoid conjugate vaccine trial: a decade of blood culture surveillance in Asante Akim North, Agogo, Ghana
papers.abstract: Long surveillance series that follow typhoid fever through a surge and its aftermath are rare in Africa. Here, we describe ten years of blood culture surveillance in Agogo, Ghana; the period included a surge in 2017 and a cluster randomised trial of a typhoid conjugate vaccine in 2021-2022. We analysed 20,035 blood cultures from febrile patients enrolled between May 2016 and December 2025 at Asante Akim North, Agogo. Periods were identified by change point detection, and changes in positivity were estimated using segmented binomial regression. With the trials household census as the denominator, we estimated detected incidence (culture confirmed cases detected per 100,000 person-years) among residents of the 15 trial communities. In total, 82 cultures (0.41%) grew Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi. Positivity rose from 2.77% (95% confidence interval 1.48-4.69) to 8.41% (6.05-11.31) during a surge between February and December 2017 and fell to 0.16% (0.11-0.22) from 2018. Thirty of 39 surge cases were children aged 5-14 years. Among residents, the detected incidence was 65.3 (45.3-91.3) per 100,000 person-years during the surge and 5.4 (2.5-10.2) in the post-surge years before vaccination. It was 5.9 (3.5-9.4) per 100,000 person-years after a campaign that vaccinated 87% of eligible children, while testing per head rose more than eight-fold. After adjustment for care seeking and blood culture sensitivity, incidence in 2016-2019 was 141 (104-189) per 100,000 person-years. Typhoid in Agogo fell sharply after 2017, three years before vaccination. Most of the later fall in test positivity reflects more testing rather than fewer cases. Thus, we recommend continued surveillance with population denominators.

papers.title: Kindergarten MMR Coverage, Vaccination Exemptions, and State-Level Measles Incidence in the United States, 2024 - 2026
papers.abstract: ObjectivesTo examine associations of kindergarten measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) coverage and vaccination exemptions with state-level measles incidence in the United States, 2024-2026. MethodsIn this ecological study of 50 states and Washington, DC (up to 153 jurisdiction-years), we linked CDC surveillance, SchoolVaxView, and Census data. Negative-binomial models estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) per percentage-point increase for completed years 2024-2025 (generalized estimating equations) and through MMWR week 39, 2024-2026 (maximum likelihood, adjusted for density and poverty). ResultsCases rose from 269 (2024) to 2,263 (2025); 3,642 were reported provisionally through October 2, 2026. Completed-year IRRs were 0.875 (95% CI=0.806, 0.950) for MMR coverage, 1.202 (1.075, 1.344) for any exemption, and 1.207 (1.059, 1.376) for nonmedical exemption. Adjusted week-39 IRRs were 0.945 (0.837, 1.068), 1.147 (1.004, 1.310), and 1.131 (0.972, 1.316). Under cluster-robust maximum likelihood, completed-year intervals for MMR coverage and nonmedical exemption included 1. ConclusionsHigher exemption prevalence was associated with greater measles incidence; other estimates were imprecise. Public Health ImplicationsMonitoring exemptions alongside MMR coverage may help identify jurisdictions needing closer vaccination-gap assessment. Ecological findings do not establish causality.

papers.title: Observed Versus Modeled Data in GLOBOCAN 2024: Variation Across Cancer Sites and Implications for the Mortality-to-Incidence Ratio
papers.abstract: PurposeThe mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) from GLOBOCAN is often used to compare cancer outcomes across countries. But in many countries, its two components come from different sources with some estimation methods deriving one from the other. We counted the countries in which both components of MIR are observed, and tested whether correlations between MIR and the Human Development Index (HDI) hold in them. MethodsUsing GLOBOCAN 2024 data, we classed a country as having independent MIR when incidence came from cancer registries, mortality was observed, and neither was derived from the other. For each of 37 cancer sites, we calculated the fraction of global new cases occurring in these countries. We compared MIR-HDI Spearman correlations ({rho}) in these countries with the full sample, testing for attenuation beyond range restriction against an HDI-matched null distribution. ResultsOnly 41 of 186 countries (22%), all with high or very high HDI, had independent MIR. Of the 144 countries with derived MIR, 131 relied on external models. The independent-MIR fraction ranged from 0.12 (Kaposi sarcoma) to 0.77 (thyroid). For 33 of 37 sites, the correlation in independent-MIR countries was within what the narrower HDI range alone would produce. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, thyroid was the only site whose correlation weakened more than the narrower HDI range would explain ({rho} -0.82 to -0.004, adjusted p = 0.011). ConclusionNo low- or medium-HDI country has independent MIR, and in 131 countries at least one MIR component comes from an external model. Comparing MIR across these countries mostly compares model inputs. In independent-MIR countries, most MIR-HDI associations are consistent with range restriction but for thyroid, the association disappears.

papers.title: Influenza activity in the United States during the 2025-26 influenza season
papers.abstract: BackgroundComprehensive influenza surveillance is conducted year-round in the United States to monitor changes in influenza activity. This report summarizes the 2025-26 U.S. influenza season. MethodsData from September 28, 2025 through October 3, 2026 were collected from national surveillance systems monitoring influenza through laboratory testing, outpatient and emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and mortality. Data modeled disease burden and assessed severity using established criteria. A subset of influenza positive specimens were genetically and antigenically characterized and assessed for antiviral susceptibility. ResultsInfluenza activity peaked during the week ending December 27, 2025, five weeks earlier than the 2024-25 season. There were two waves of influenza activity with influenza A(H3N2) subclade K viruses predominating the season overall and during the first wave followed by a smaller B/Victoria wave. The majority of circulating A(H3N2) and B/Victoria viruses were antigenically drifted from 2025-26 influenza vaccine reference strains. Season severity was classified as moderate overall, with children (0-17 years old) experiencing a high severity season and adults experiencing a moderate severity season. Children experienced the highest percent of influenza-associated outpatient and emergency department visits compared to other age groups. This seasons cumulative influenza-associated hospitalization rate in children is the highest hospitalization rate in the past 16 years. Additionally, there were 198 influenza-associated pediatric deaths reported to CDC as of October 29, 2026. ConclusionsAlthough antigenically drifted A(H3N2) viruses predominated, the 2025-26 U.S. influenza season occurred within historic norms for timing and severity. Year-round surveillance remains critical for detecting changes in influenza viruses and monitoring influenza-associated morbidity and mortality. Key PointsO_LICDCs severity assessment framework classified the 2025-26 U.S. influenza season as moderate across all age groups C_LIO_LINationally, peak influenza activity occurred in late December 2025 C_LIO_LIInfluenza A(H3N2) subclade K viruses predominated during the 2025-26 season C_LI

papers.title: Colorectal cancer incidence and mortality trends by age at onset in South Africa from 2002 to 2023
papers.abstract: BackgroundColorectal cancer is the third most common cancer in men and women, and the fifth most common cancer overall, in South Africa. A previous report by the South African National Cancer Registry (SANCR) established that colorectal cancer incidence is rising in all South African population groups but rising fastest in Black South Africans. However, whether incidence increases by age at onset, as observed in many upper-income countries worldwide, remains unknown. In the present study, we assessed changes in colorectal cancer incidence (2002-2023) and mortality (2002-2019) in South Africa by sex, population group and age at onset. MethodsWe calculated incidence from SANCR case counts and mortality from Stats SA death records, using Stats SA mid-year population estimates, standardised to the Segi world standard population. We defined age at onset as early (<50 years) or late ([≥]50 years). We described trends using joinpoint regression and annual percentage changes (APCs) over 2002-2023 and 2011- 2023, the period after private-laboratory reporting became mandatory. ResultsA total of 70,467 histologically confirmed primary colorectal cancers were registered with the SANCR over 2002-2023; 53.7% were in men. The overall age-standardised incidence rate (ASIR) was 6.61 per 100,000 (95% CI 6.32-6.89) in 2002 and 8.23 (7.99-8.46) in 2023. Overall incidence fell from 2002 to 2007 (not significant), rose from 2007 to 2015 and showed no significant change from 2015 to 2023. The first two segments coincide with the withdrawal of some private laboratories from reporting in 2005-2007 and with mandatory reporting from 2011. From 2011 to 2023, incidence fell in White South Africans (APC -1.0%, 95% CI -1.9 to -0.04), rose in Black African South Africans (+3.1%, 2.0 to 4.2) and did not change significantly in Coloured (-1.0%, -2.3 to 0.3) or Indian/Asian (+0.3%, -2.2 to 2.7) South Africans. Early-onset incidence rose by 1.6% per year (95% CI 1.1 to 2.1) over 2002-2023, similar to late-onset incidence (1.8%, 1.0 to 2.5). After 2011, neither changed significantly (early-onset +0.3%, -0.3 to 0.9; late-onset 0.0%, -1.0 to 1.0). Over 2002-2023, the early-onset APC was highest in White South Africans (+3.9%, 2.9 to 4.9), followed by Black African (+1.7%, 1.1 to 2.4), Coloured (+1.6%, 1.0 to 2.3) and Indian/Asian (+1.5%, 0.4 to 2.7) South Africans. The late-onset APC was +4.1% (3.4 to 4.9) in Black African, +1.3% (0.1 to 2.5) in White, +1.3% (0.1 to 2.5) in Indian/Asian and +0.7% (-0.3 to 1.6) in Coloured South Africans. After 2011, early-onset incidence rose in White (+1.2%, 0.3 to 2.2), Coloured (+1.7%, 0.4 to 3.1) and Black African (+1.1%, 0.4 to 1.8) South Africans. Late-onset incidence fell in White South Africans (-1.5%, -2.6 to -0.4) and rose in Black African South Africans (+3.7%, 2.4 to 5.0). Early-onset mortality rose by 1.2% per year (0.5 to 2.0) over 2002-2019, and late-onset mortality by 0.9% (0.3 to 1.4). ConclusionEarly-onset colorectal cancer incidence in South Africa rose over 2002-2023, and much of the rise coincided with mandatory private-laboratory reporting from 2011. Since 2011, early-onset incidence has risen modestly in White, Coloured and Black African South Africans, while late-onset incidence has fallen in White South Africans. In Black African South Africans, late-onset incidence and mortality continue to rise faster than early-onset.

papers.title: The plateau in liver disease mortality in Germany: contrasting trends by age, region and ICD-10 code, 2000-2024
papers.abstract: BackgroundCirrhosis is often diagnosed only at decompensation, making identification of high-risk groups important for prevention and early detection. Chronic liver disease mortality has fallen in southern Europe and France since 2010, but not in Germany. Whether the German plateau reflects birth-cohort alcohol exposure, metabolic liver disease or certification practice is unknown. MethodsDeaths by ICD-10 code, sex and age group were extracted from the WHO Mortality Database for 16 European countries (2000-2022), with Eurostat rates (2011-2023), German state-level mortality (1998-2024) and hospital diagnoses (2000-2023). Registry and Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023 estimates were summarised for ages 45-64, 65-74 and 75 years and over, with registry rates standardised to the European Standard Population 2013. FindingsGermanys age-standardised chronic liver disease mortality was 16.6 per 100 000 in 2011 and 16.0 in 2023, against declines of 21-37% in France, Italy and Spain. Between 2010 and 2022, alcoholic liver disease mortality at ages 45-64 fell by 17% in men and 25% in women, whereas fibrosis and cirrhosis (K74) mortality at ages 65-74 rose by 27% and 28%, with larger K70-K77 mortality increases in eastern than western Germany. Hospitalisation rates showed similar age-specific patterns, while in-hospital case fatality declined. Fewer than 0.5% of liver deaths were certified as fatty liver. GBD 2023 showed a similar age-specific increase but attributed rising mortality to all five modelled aetiologies. InterpretationThe German plateau reflects continued decline below age 65 and rising mortality at ages 65-74, compatible with cohorts born 1945-59 reaching this age band, particularly in eastern Germany. Consumption records and surveys indicate differing regional patterns of alcohol exposure. Much of the cirrhosis in these cohorts is certified without aetiology, and GBDs aetiological estimates cannot be verified in registration data. FundingNone. Research in context Evidence before this studyPubMed was searched without language restriction from inception to October 15, 2026, for registry-based analyses of cirrhosis or chronic liver disease mortality in Germany or in European comparisons, and for comparisons of GBD estimates with vital registration, using combinations of the terms cirrhosis, liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, mortality, Germany, Europe, age-period-cohort, Global Burden of Disease and vital registration. Registry analyses have documented an east-to-west gradient of cirrhosis mortality across Europe and, in Germany, period and birth-cohort effects on alcohol-related mortality, with lower risks in later-born cohorts. A nationwide hospital study reported rising admissions for cirrhosis with falling in-hospital mortality. GBD publications acknowledge that ICD coding cannot reliably distinguish cirrhosis aetiologies, which are assigned using statistical models. We found no previous study combining detailed ICD-10 mortality analyses, age-specific European comparison, German federal-state trends and comparison with GBD aetiological estimates. Added value of this studyWe compared GBD 2023 estimates with European mortality registration data and examined German mortality by detailed ICD-10 code, age, sex and federal state, alongside hospital diagnosis statistics. The German plateau reflects rising mortality at 65-74 years, especially in eastern Germany, while mortality continues to decline at 45-64 years. The increase was concentrated in deaths coded as unspecified cirrhosis (K74.6) and accompanied by rising cirrhosis hospitalisation rates. At the same time, in-hospital case fatality and admissions for chronic viral hepatitis declined. GBD identified a similar age-specific increase but estimated rising mortality for all five aetiological sub-causes despite their differing representation in routine data. Implications of all the available evidenceThe absence of a decline in cirrhosis mortality in Germany is consistent with older birth cohorts with high cumulative alcohol exposure, although the aetiology of cirrhosis is often unspecified. Differences in alcohol consumption patterns, obesity and conditions after reunification may contribute to higher mortality in parts of eastern Germany. The findings support earlier detection and improved treatment access for older adults, age-specific surveillance in Germany and other European countries, and cautious interpretation of modelled aetiological fractions in countries without multiple-cause mortality data.

papers.title: Delivered but Discharged Without Assessment: A National Multilevel Analysis of Missed Maternal Postpartum Assessment Before Discharge After Facility Birth in Ethiopia, 2024/2025 EDHS
papers.abstract: BackgroundMissed maternal postpartum assessment before discharge after facility birth is an under-measured indicator of intrafacility quality of care that previous Ethiopian studies did not isolate in nationally representative analyses. This gap matters because women may reach facilities for childbirth yet leave without a basic maternal clinical assessment during the highest-risk postpartum period. MethodsWe analyzed national 2024-2025 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey data for 3,645 women aged 15-49 years whose most recent live birth occurred in a health facility. Analyses incorporated sampling weights and complex survey design. Factors associated with missed assessment were examined using multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression accounting for enumeration-area clustering. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. ResultsOverall, 40.1% (95% CI: 37.0-43.3) of women delivering in health facilities did not receive a maternal postpartum assessment before discharge. Missed assessment was less likely following caesarean birth than vaginal delivery (AOR 0.32, 95% CI: 0.19-0.53) and among women with pregnancy complications (AOR 0.46, 95% CI: 0.34-0.63). Antenatal care showed a dose-response association, with lower odds among women with 4-7 visits (AOR 0.49, 95% CI: 0.27-0.89) and [≥]8 visits (AOR 0.43, 95% CI: 0.23-0.81) compared with no ANC. Geographic inequities persisted, including higher odds in Somali (AOR 2.07, 95% CI: 1.02-4.18). ConclusionsA substantial proportion of facility births in Ethiopia end without a maternal assessment before discharge, indicating that institutional delivery coverage can overestimate effective postpartum care when discharge processes are weak.

papers.title: Cross-informant validation of the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview in adolescents: Agreement between child and parent reports
papers.abstract: BackgroundReliable assessment of avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) in young people may require information from both children and caregivers, yet cross-informant agreement has not been examined for the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview (PARDI). This study evaluated agreement between child and parent PARDI interviews for ARFID diagnosis, individual DSM-5 Criterion A, ARFID dimensions, and overall severity. MethodsTwenty children aged 11-14 years screening positive for ARFID and one parent per child were recruited from the ARFID InitiativE Sweden (ARIES) cohort. Children and parents completed separate PARDI interviews with trained interviewers. Parent-child agreement was assessed using percentage agreement and Cohens kappa ({kappa}) for categorical ratings of ARFID diagnosis and Criterion A consequences. For continuous ratings of ARFID dimensions and overall severity, agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and paired t-tests comparing mean parent and child scores. ResultsParents gave higher mean scores than children across all continuous domains, although the difference was statistically significant only for overall severity (raw mean difference=0.42, p=.003). Parent-child agreement was poor for sensory sensitivity (ICC=0.42), moderate for lack of interest (ICC=0.63) and overall severity (ICC=0.71), and excellent for concern about aversive consequences (ICC=0.95). ARFID was identified in 17/20 parent interviews and 14/20 child interviews; diagnostic agreement was 75% ({kappa}=0.31, p=.133). Agreement was perfect (100%) for Criterion A1, high for A2 and A3 (both 95%), and lowest for psychosocial impairment (A4; 65% agreement, {kappa}=0.19). Item-level findings indicated a general tendency toward higher parental ratings, although children provided higher ratings on selected items involving food restriction, sensory experiences, hunger cues, and abdominal pain. ConclusionsChild and parent PARDI interviews provided overlapping but non-interchangeable information. Agreement varied across different aspects of ARFID, with greater discrepancies for psychosocial impairment and sensory sensitivity. These differences may partly reflect what children and parents are able to observe or experience directly. Multi-informant assessment may therefore offer a more complete account of pediatric ARFID than either response alone. Plain English SummaryChildren may experience and describe avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) symptoms differently from how their parents observe and report them. We compared separate child and parent diagnostic interviews using the Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview (PARDI) in 20 pairs to understand how closely their assessments of ARFID agreed. Parents and children often provided similar information, but agreement differed depending on what was being assessed. They agreed more closely about effects on weight, growth, and nutrition, and about fears of aversive consequences of eating such as choking or vomiting. Agreement was lower for how eating difficulties affected daily and social life, for lack of interest in food or eating, and for sensitivity to the taste, texture, or smell of food. Parents generally rated the overall severity of eating difficulties higher than children, although children gave higher ratings for some experiences, such as difficulty recognizing hunger, discomfort with messy or sticky foods, and fear of abdominal pain. These findings suggest that children and parents provide overlapping but not identical information about ARFID. Child and parent accounts may each highlight different aspects of ARFID, making both perspectives valuable sources of information during assessment.

papers.title: Widening racial and ethnic disparities in Helicobacter pylori infection in the United States: a Bayesian meta-analytic catalytic model of age-specific forces of infection
papers.abstract: BackgroundHelicobacter pylori is the main cause of non-cardia gastric cancer. In the U.S. H. pylori seroprevalence has declined. However, whether all subgroups have benefited equally from this change is unclear. Further, prevalence alone cannot indicate when infection risk is most acute and thus when to target prevention efforts like screening. MethodsWe synthesized age-stratified H. pylori seroprevalence data from 36 U.S. studies (N=56,845; 1965-2014), identified via literature search through September 2022. We fitted Bayesian hierarchical catalytic epidemic models to estimate, by race/ethnicity (for each of five race/ethnicity groups) and birth cohort (pre-1960 vs. 1960+, or continuous), the maximum proportion infected, age-specific force of infection (FOI), and the age at half-maximum seroprevalence. FindingsDisparities in maximum prevalence worsened in the 1960+ birth cohort, with the absolute Hispanic-Non-Hispanic White (NHW) gap widening from 33.2 to 51.4 percentage points. FOIs peaked at the youngest ages for the Non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) and Non-Hispanic Black (NHB) populations. Age patterns varied independently of burden; Hispanic and AI/AN populations reached similar peak prevalence (83.0% vs 76.1%) for the 1960+ birth cohort, yet the age at half-maximum seroprevalence was 19.3 years (95%CrI: 14.9, 23.5) vs 3.20 years (95%CrI: 1.99, 4.63). Continuous birth-cohort analyses supported these findings. InterpretationNational declines in H. pylori mask widening racial and ethnic disparities. In AI/AN and NHB populations, seroprevalence rises steeply in early childhood, well before adulthood-targeted screen-and-treat programs would intervene. Moreover, similar peak prevalence can mask different age patterns of infection, and should be accounted for when guiding prevention strategies. FundingNational Cancer Institute U01CA265729 and U01CA319219 Research in ContextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSWe used studies reporting Helicobacter pylori seroprevalence in U.S. populations from a recent systematic scoping review covering publications through 2022. Reported U.S. seroprevalence has declined over successive birth cohorts, and prevalence is consistently higher among Hispanic, Non-Hispanic Black, American Indian and Alaska Native, and Asian and Pacific Islander populations than among non-Hispanic White populations. Recent estimates mainly derive from limited populations, such as veterans or single integrated health systems. American Indian, Alaska Native, Asian, and Pacific Islander participants are also often grouped into a single "other" category. Catalytic epidemic models have been used to estimate age-specific force of infection for H. pylori in Mexico, Japan, and in a recent analysis of two NHANES cycles. However, none of these studies have estimated forces of infection separately for all five Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results program (SEER) racial and ethnic groups in the U.S. or across more than two survey periods. There has also been a lack of quantitative evidence for differences in the approximate age distribution of infection risk across race/ethnic groups and birth cohorts and how racial disparities in infection burden have changed over time. Added value of the studyWe applied modified catalytic epidemic models to estimate age-specific prevalence and rates of infection for each of the five race/ethnic SEER categories and by birth cohort. To additionally probe differences in when infection is typically concentrated by race/ethnicity and birth cohort group, we computed the age at which each group reaches half its maximum seroprevalence. Our approach pools data across distinct study sources and populations, accommodates study-specific heterogeneity and variation between race/ethnicity groups, and improves estimates in data-limited groups. Importantly, we improve the robustness of our key findings by applying a range of model extensions that accommodate distinct latent assumptions in catalytic epidemic models, namely the fundamental nature of the relationship between forces of infection and age and birth cohort effects. Our results reaffirm notable absolute and relative disparities in predicted prevalence and the risk of infection among race/ethnic minority groups, which have been intensified in more recent birth cohorts. We also demonstrate that infection trajectories maintain relatively distinct (early-age or later-onset) age trends across race/ethnic groups and within the same subgroup across birth cohorts. Implications of all the available evidenceThere is an ever-increasing need for evaluating expanded screen-and-treat programs for H. pylori, as population-level declines in prevalence have concealed notable worsening disparities in burden across race/ethnic groups. Screening strategies should be tailored to population-specific age-specific patterns in infection risk, with testing prioritized in early life where seroprevalence rises steeply in childhood, as in AI/AN and Non-Hispanic Black populations, and at first clinical contact for immigrants from high-incidence regions, whose infections likely predate arrival.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 antibody landscape following multiple vaccinations and infections during Omicron period
papers.abstract: BackgroundRepeated COVID-19 vaccination effects on the immunogenicity, breadth, and durability of antibody responses across antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants remain incompletely understood. MethodParticipants receiving [≥]five COVID-19 vaccine doses 2020-2025 were selected from a prospective cohort in Michigan. Serum IgG, IgM, and ACE2 percent inhibition were measured using multiplex assays. Baseline-adjusted immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, and formulation-specific antibody durability were evaluated using regression models. ResultTwenty-one participants were included (median: seven vaccine doses). For every two-fold increase in pre-vaccination IgG concentration, post-vaccination fold-rise was 34% (95% CI: 16%-48%), 43% (95% CI: 15%-62%), and 55% (95% CI: 21%-75%) lower following monovalent, bivalent, and 2023- 24 vaccination, while baseline-adjusted immunogenicity showed no significant trends across successive vaccines. Antibody landscapes demonstrated broad cross-reactivity against ancestral and Omicron variants, with similar strain-specific IgG changes across ancestral, vaccine-matched, and antigenically distant strains, but greater heterogeneity in ACE2 inhibition. Formulation-specific waning models showed significant IgG declines following monovalent and bivalent vaccination ({beta} = -1.03, 95% CI: -1.51 to -0.55; P<0.001 and -1.00, 95% CI: -1.71 to -0.30; P=0.007, respectively) and ACE2 inhibition declines following monovalent vaccination, while other formulations showed less consistent changes. Despite waning, antibody levels generally remained relatively high across variants up to 300 days post-vaccination, with formulation-specific differences in durability. ConclusionRepeated COVID-19 vaccination maintained baseline-adjusted immunogenicity and broad cross-reactive antibody responses, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Higher baseline immunity was associated with smaller post-vaccination increases, suggesting repeated boosting continues to reinforce humoral immunity despite increasingly complex immune histories.

papers.title: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis Rates Among High-Risk Populations in Brazil: An Analysis from 2001 to 2021
authors: C. Dailton Guedes de Oliveira Moraes
papers.abstract: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) represents a global public health threat, with a rising prevalence, particularly among vulnerable populations. This cross-sectional study analyzed MDR-TB notifications in Brazil from 2001 to 2021, using data from DATASUS, and stratified by periods and risk groups (HIV-positive individuals, smokers, drug users, healthcare workers, incarcerated individuals, and people experiencing homelessness). Descriptive analyses and parametric statistical tests (ANOVA and Tukey, p<0.05) were applied. A significant increase in cases was observed across all groups, especially between 2017 and 2021, with growth ranging from 294% to 574% depending on the population. Factors such as treatment abandonment, coinfection, social vulnerability, and occupational exposure were key determinants for MDR-TB dissemination. The findings indicate that current public health policies are insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for targeted prevention strategies, therapeutic follow-up, and control measures for high-risk populations.

papers.title: Multi-omics models for hypertension prediction using blood pressure PRS and omics scores
papers.abstract: BackgroundHypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the relative contributions of proteomic (ProtS), metabolomic (MetS), and polygenic risk scores (PRS) to incident hypertension risk remain incompletely characterized. MethodsWe developed ProtS and MetS for systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and hypertension using Elastic Net regression in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). We incorporated these scores with previously developed BP PRSs into 5 incremental XGBoost models, with external validation in the Jackson Heart Study (JHS). We further applied transfer learning to adapt the MESA-derived models to JHS. Elastic Net selected proteins were prioritized using Mendelian randomization, colocalization, and functional analyses. ResultsIn MESA, model discrimination improved with the addition of omics scores, with the combined model achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.72 compared with 0.63 for the clinical baseline model. In JHS, ProtS showed the highest AUC of 0.68 and the smallest cross-cohort performance decline, compared to MetS and PRS. Incorporating measured SBP and DBP substantially improved discrimination, with the PRS+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.80 in MESA and the baseline+BP model achieving an AUC of 0.74 in JHS. Among JHS participants with normal baseline BP, ProtS provided the strongest discrimination among models without measured BP (AUC = 0.62), while PRS+BP model achieved an AUC of 0.69. Leaf-weight refreshing consistently improved calibration in JHS while preserving discrimination. Mendelian randomization identified 77 proteins associated with BP traits or hypertension, involved in vascular, inflammatory, renal, and natriuretic pathways. ConclusionsProtS demonstrated superior predictive performance and cross-cohort transferability among the omics modalities evaluated, while measured BP remained the strongest predictors of incident hypertension. Proteomic and genetic information may provide complementary biological signals for identifying individuals at elevated hypertension risk, particularly before clinically elevated BP is detectable.

papers.title: Beyond National Averages: Social Contact Patterns in the Upper Midwest
papers.abstract: BackgroundSocial contact surveys measure how individuals interact with each other, which directly influences disease transmission dynamics. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered how people live and work, highlighting the need for up-to-date and sub-national estimates of social contact patterns to inform disease modeling and public health planning. MethodsThe Midwest Analytics & Disease Modeling Center (MADMC) conducted an opt-in social contact survey of upper Midwest residents, with about 60% of participants drawn from Minnesota. Participants reported all interpersonal contacts during the previous day, including the age of their contacts allowing for the analysis of mixing patterns. Detailed demographic information about the participants was also collected, allowing for additional subgroup analyses of contact patterns. ResultsParticipants in our sample had an average of 6.8 contacts per day (IQR: 2.0 - 8.0), which is within the range of recent post-pandemic US national and European estimates. Contacts varied across demographic groups, with those attending work or school in-person reporting the highest number of contacts. Mixing across most age group pairs was a little lower than in comparable national survey except for younger age groups, who had substantially higher rates of contact with same-age peers. Differences in the contact matrices alone were associated with a 6.7% difference in estimated basic reproduction number(R0). Near the epidemic threshold, even this modest difference could meaningfully affect transmission dynamics. These effects may be amplified or attenuated by pathogen-specific age patterns of susceptibility and infectiousness, leading to larger or smaller differences in R0 estimates derived from national versus regional mixing patterns. ConclusionsThese findings provide empirical evidence on post-pandemic social contact patterns in the United States and highlight the potential implications of regional variation in social mixing for infectious disease transmission. The mean 6.8 daily contacts is consistent with evidence of persistent changes in daily routines following the pandemic. Incorporating contemporary, region-specific contact patterns into transmission models may improve their ability to capture geographic variation in transmission risk and inform epidemic forecasting.

papers.title: Wastewater sequence data reveal national and cross-border virus transmission dynamics
papers.abstract: Spatial epidemic models estimate disease transmission counts between populations using human mobility data, but location-to-location transmission is rarely observed directly. To address this gap, we develop mutation-counting methods to infer transmission structure from viral genetic variation measured in wastewater. In epidemic simulations with known transmission networks, our primary estimator robustly recovers spatial structure under realistic mutation-detection limits. Applied to spatiotemporal SARS-CoV-2 wastewater data from Austria, the method reveals strong seasonal reorganization, with inferred transmission becoming more geographically localized in winter and more dispersed in summer. We further identify locations with systematically higher or lower connectivity than expected from commuting, with temporal changes coinciding with regional restrictions, reopening and tourism. We then test whether such inference remains possible across national borders, recovering coherent spatial structure and temporal variation in connectivity between Austria, Switzerland and Liechtenstein. These results establish wastewater sequence data as a promising complement to mobility data for monitoring spatial transmission and detecting changes in epidemic spread associated with seasonality and interventions.
